text:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: spike in 5xx and request timeouts for variant 'llama-slim-v2-quant' across us-west-2 (elevated errors 5xx: 18% -> 47% in 5m). paging oncall. thread=1897654321

Maria O. (oncall): I'm on it. Looking at traces and recent deploys. any deploys in last 30m?

Samir K. (sre): No deploys to the serving runtime in the last hour. I see a sudden increase in KV cache misses and memory pressure on the v2 hosts. Also a surge of long-context requests hitting v2 (mostly seq_len > 2048).

Alice N. (ml): v2 has a quantized codepath that regresses under long sequences sometimes. We'll try to confirm. Can we route traffic off v2 while we investigate?

Maria O. (oncall): We should mitigate live traffic first. Proposed plan: 1) emergency throttle heavy keys 2) set variant weight to 0 for llama-slim-v2 3) route traffic to llama-slim-v1-stable as fallback. Any objections? :+1: or :-1:?

Jeremy S. (support): Multiple customers reporting generation truncation and 502s. Top affected keys: key_8F3, key_A99, key_XT4. Customer-visible impact estimated ~ 12 API keys, some high-qps. Please escalate to product for comms if we keep routing change >15m.

Lina P. (product): Acknowledged. Prep a short status note for affected customers if mitigation isn't immediate. Also we should track regression tests to verify v2 fix before re-enabling.

Samir K. (sre): Executing emergency throttles on heavy keys now. Commands I ran:

```
# throttle heavy keys to 1 rps and reduce burst
rlctl set --api-key key_8F3 --rps 1 --burst 1 --reason "emergency-throttle-llama-slim-v2"
rlctl set --api-key key_A99 --rps 1 --burst 1 --reason "emergency-throttle-llama-slim-v2"
rlctl set --api-key key_XT4 --rps 1 --burst 1 --reason "emergency-throttle-llama-slim-v2"
```

Samir K. (sre): Throttles applied. Observed immediate reduction in p99 latency from 1.9s to 750ms for those keys. But overall 5xx still high ~32%.

Maria O. (oncall): Next: disable variant routing. We'll move weight to 0 for llama-slim-v2 and pin fallback to v1-stable. I'll run the routing change and DeployBot will confirm. Command below (internal API):

```
# set variant weight to 0 and force fallback
curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/routing/llama-slim -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"variants": [{"name":"v2-quant","weight":0},{"name":"v1-stable","weight":100}], "reason":"emergency_disable_v2_1897654321"}'
```

DeployBot: Deploy change accepted. rolling routing update to edge nodes...

DeployBot: Routing update complete. v2 weight=0 -> traffic now served by v1-stable.

Maria O. (oncall): Observing system metrics... 5xx rate dropped to 3.2% in the last 2m. Latency stabilized. Customer error reports decreasing. :white_check_mark:

Alice N. (ml): Good signal. We'll reproduce locally with long sequences against v2-quant and collect a trace dump. Please capture any heap snapshots from affected hosts and metrics for attention ops.

Samir K. (sre): Captured heap + logs from host group llama-slim-v2-quant-usw2-*. Uploading to /artifacts/incidents/INC-2026-345/ for triage. Also opened a temporary circuit-breaker rule to prevent v2 from receiving new traffic even if config flips accidentally: `cbctl create --name disallow-llama-slim-v2 --target variant:v2-quant --action block`

Jeremy S. (support): Logged affected customers and created support tickets for each. Copying product and account teams. Will send a short status note: "We temporarily routed traffic to a stable variant due to elevated errors; no data loss; working on a fix; timeline TBD."

Lina P. (product): Approve comms. Use the incident page: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2026-345 for updates. Add the expected customer impact summary (12 keys, primarily lower throughput but decreased errors).

Maria O. (oncall): Immediate mitigation complete. Next actions: - ML to root cause v2 regression and propose fix/patch - SRE to validate fix on canary with controlled traffic - Product/Support to coordinate comms - Keep circuit-breaker in place until v2 passes regression suite

Alice N. (ml): Starting root cause. Early hypothesis: quantized attention kernel under long context causing memory corruption leading to transient failures. We'll instrument and test with a smaller replica set. ETA for initial findings: 2 hours.

Samir K. (sre): Adding monitoring alerts: decrease allowed rollout % for v2, add a regression alert tied to 5xx > 5% for 10m. Also pinned auto-scaler to avoid spinning up more v2 hosts.

Maria O. (oncall): Handoff: I'm on for 30 more minutes to verify stabilization, then handing to night oncall @Samir K. (sre). Samir — please pick up and keep an eye on the incident channel. If errors creep above 5% re-open and escalate.

Samir K. (sre): Acknowledged. I'll continue monitoring. Logging follow-up tasks in the incident ticket and scheduling a postmortem after resolution.

DeployBot: note: routing change rolled back automatically in 00:00:00? no, no rollback. All good.

Incident Bot: Incident INC-2026-345 created and assigned. Priority: P1. Timeline notes attached.

Maria O. (oncall): Thanks team — mitigation worked, customers improving. We'll reconvene after ML posts a root-cause update. Closing active mitigation steps in this thread. :white_check_mark:

Lina P. (product): Please flag if we need to publish an external incident postmortem. I want to coordinate messaging with legal for enterprise customers.

Alice N. (ml): Will post RCA and patch plan in the incident ticket within 4-6 hours. After patch verified, we'll rehearse a controlled canary re-enable with 1% traffic.

Samir K. (sre): Leaving final note: emergency throttles and variant disable were the right live mitigations. Keep circuit-breaker until patch validated.

Jeremy S. (support): Sending update to affected customers now.

Maria O. (oncall): Handoff complete, marking thread as monitored.
